meta.basis: 100 synthetic domain validation cases rewritten from internet research across FHA/HUD Handbook 4000.1 appraisal/MPR guidance, VA Pamphlet 26-7 MPR and concession guidance, Fannie Mae IPC/property-condition/site-utility rules, Freddie Mac seller contribution guidance, and CFPB closing-disclosure seller-credit references.
meta.warning: These are internet-researched synthetic cases, not verified customer interviews or legal, lending, appraisal, or underwriting advice.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD appraisal guidance treats utility availability as a prerequisite to observing major systems.
cases.deal: FHA purchase of vacant winterized house; appraisal is scheduled before seller turns on utilities.
expectedLeadScope: possible reinspection after systems are active
lender warning that hidden repair conditions may surface
cases.requiredGate: FHA appraisal scheduling and utility activation confirmation
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may ask for a cosmetic credit while missing a lender-visible condition that can delay closing.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD mechanical-system review can require follow-up when water service prevents plumbing and hot-water observation.
cases.deal: FHA buyer under contract on an estate sale with water off until municipal account transfer.
expectedLeadScope: water restoration before appraisal or reinspection
water heater operation once service is active
cases.riskIfWrong: A closing-cost-credit draft can understate that the appraiser may not clear the property without operating water.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD appraisal practice requires observable heating function when gas service is needed for a permanent heat source.
cases.deal: FHA buyer; seller turned off gas after moving out.
expectedLeadScope: possible HVAC service call if furnace fails startup
cases.requiredGate: FHA permanent heat and utility operation gate
cases.riskIfWrong: The response may suggest accepting portable heaters even though financing depends on a lender-acceptable heat source.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD MPR concepts prioritize electrical hazards that affect occupant safety.
cases.deal: FHA buyer with inspection contingency open and appraisal not yet completed.
cases.requiredGate: qualified electrical quote and lender disclosure check
cases.riskIfWrong: Treating electrical hazards as a normal credit can leave a required repair unresolved at appraisal.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD minimum property standards require the dwelling to be safely habitable, including adequate permanent heat where needed.
cases.deal: FHA purchase in January; seller says wall plug heaters are enough until spring.
expectedLeadScope: permanent heating system repair or replacement
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer could negotiate a cosmetic allowance while the loan remains blocked by habitability.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD appliance and mechanical guidance distinguishes market-value systems from preference items.
cases.deal: FHA buyer; appraiser likely to observe central cooling because the system remains with the home.
cases.requiredGate: FHA appraiser and lender treatment of cooling failure
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may over-ask on preferences and under-call a built-in system that affects value and marketability.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD living-unit standards focus on basic kitchen water and cooking utility capability, not cosmetic appliance upgrades.
cases.deal: FHA purchase of tenant-occupied home with basic kitchen defects.
cases.riskIfWrong: A repair packet may chase appliance preferences instead of conditions needed for loan insurability.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD appraisal guidance can require appliances that remain and contribute to value to be operational.
cases.deal: FHA buyer; contract includes built-in range and dishwasher.
cases.requiredGate: appliance inclusion and value-contribution check with lender
cases.riskIfWrong: The answer may assume all appliance issues are optional, causing a surprise appraisal condition.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD MPR risk is high when a roof leak affects soundness and interior moisture.
cases.deal: FHA buyer; roof leak was visible before appraisal.
expectedLeadScope: interior water intrusion tied to roof
expectedExclusions: loose gutter downspout unless tied to water intrusion
cases.requiredGate: roof contractor evidence before lender/Appraiser clearance
cases.riskIfWrong: Calling it a simple closing credit may fail because lender-visible roof leakage usually needs repair evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD roof analysis can trigger replacement or repair when remaining utility is inadequate or leaks are probable.
cases.deal: FHA purchase with 22-year-old shingles and appraiser visit next week.
expectedLeadScope: missing shingle repair or replacement scope
expectedExclusions: cosmetic moss unless roof performance is affected
cases.requiredGate: roofing professional quote plus FHA lender review
cases.riskIfWrong: A buyer may accept a small credit that cannot cure a roof condition before closing.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD defective-paint standards create lender-visible risk for pre-1978 dwellings.
cases.persona: Buyer agent in older housing stock
cases.deal: FHA buyer on 1924 home; seller prefers a credit instead of paint work.
cases.requiredGate: pre-1978 paint protocol and lender/appraiser signoff
cases.riskIfWrong: A credit-only request may leave a known FHA repair condition unresolved.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD appraisal guidance can treat exterior paint exposing substrate as a repair issue even outside lead-based-paint framing.
cases.deal: FHA appraisal on a 1992 house with neglected exterior trim.
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may dismiss all paint as cosmetic and miss a required exterior repair.

findings: missing handrail at five exterior steps

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD site safety review can require correction of exposed hazards before insurance endorsement.

cases.deal: VA purchase in small HOA-run water district.

cases.deal: VA purchase near visible utility corridor.

cases.sourceBasis: VA appraisal process can require marketability and insurance attention when flood risk is present.

cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may negotiate ordinary repairs while failing to clear mandatory flood insurance or collateral questions.

cases.sourceBasis: VA MPR habitability and appraisal review can flag non-permitted conversions lacking safe heat, egress, or utility support.

findings: space heated by extension cord heater
expectedLeadScope: legal and safe use of converted area
appraisal treatment of unpermitted living area
cases.riskIfWrong: The output may value the space as ordinary bedroom area and miss collateral eligibility risk.

cases.sourceBasis: VA MPR defect guidance treats abnormal settlement and moisture intrusion as structural/safety concerns.
cases.deal: VA buyer; inspection found basement movement.
cases.requiredGate: qualified structural/moisture report and VA lender acceptance
cases.riskIfWrong: A credit request may be inadequate if the NOV requires correction or professional clearance.

cases.sourceBasis: VA seller-concession guidance separates ordinary closing costs from the 4 percent concession bucket.
cases.persona: VA buyer agent negotiating seller help
cases.deal: VA buyer asks seller for closing-cost help and prepaid insurance.
findings: seller to pay all allowable closing costs
seller to prepay one year hazard insurance
seller to pay VA funding fee
home inspection noted minor paint chips
expectedLeadScope: separate closing-cost credits from VA concessions
track prepaid insurance and funding fee against concession cap
expectedExclusions: minor paint chips unless appraisal/MPR sensitive
cases.riskIfWrong: Combining all seller payments into one bucket can either kill a valid credit or exceed VA limits.

cases.sourceBasis: VA guidance caps concessions such as funding fee payments, debt payoff, and certain prepaids by reasonable value.
cases.deal: VA buyer wants seller to pay funding fee and two credit cards to improve qualification.
findings: seller payoff of buyer credit-card debt
expectedExclusions: new appliances unless contract/lender treats as concession
cases.requiredGate: VA lender concession approval after appraisal value
cases.riskIfWrong: The deal may be written with benefits the VA lender must reject or restructure.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC limits cap financing concessions by occupancy and LTV/CLTV tier.
cases.deal: Conventional primary residence at 95 percent LTV; buyer asks for 5 percent seller credit.
findings: seller wants to keep price unchanged
expectedLeadScope: 3 percent IPC cap risk for high-LTV primary
credit cannot exceed buyer closing costs
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may draft an amendment the lender must reduce or treat as a sales concession.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC guidance allows a higher cap for primary/second-home transactions in the mid-LTV tier, but still limits use.
cases.deal: Conventional primary at 82 percent LTV; seller offers 7 percent credit to preserve price.
findings: buyer has 5 percent actual closing costs
seller asks credit to cover furniture
expectedExclusions: minor HVAC age concern if system functions
cases.riskIfWrong: Excess credits may require price reduction, LTV recalculation, or loan restructuring.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC limits for low-LTV principal residences do not allow unused credit to become cash to buyer.
cases.deal: Conventional primary at 70 percent LTV; seller agrees to 9 percent credit but buyer costs are only 3 percent.
findings: closing costs far below credit amount
buyer wants unused amount after closing
expectedExclusions: minor plumbing drip unless active damage or lender-visible
cases.riskIfWrong: The output could imply the buyer can receive leftover seller money, creating disclosure and eligibility risk.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC limits are materially lower for investment properties.
cases.deal: Conventional investment purchase; buyer asks for 4 percent seller credit for rate buydown.
expectedLeadScope: buydown cost counted as financing concession
expectedExclusions: tenant carpet preference unless safety/habitability issue
cases.requiredGate: investment-property IPC cap and buydown approval
cases.riskIfWrong: A primary-residence credit assumption can make the loan unsalable or force a late amendment.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC tiers apply to second homes similarly to principal residences but depend on LTV/CLTV.

expectedLeadScope: 3 percent IPC cap for high-CLTV second home
expectedExclusions: dock boards weathered unless safety or collateral condition
cases.riskIfWrong: Using the wrong LTV tier may overstate allowable seller help by thousands of dollars.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC guidance does not permit interested-party money to satisfy borrower down payment or minimum contribution.
cases.deal: Conventional buyer short on down payment asks seller to credit funds toward the 5 percent down.
findings: seller credit described as down payment help
expectedLeadScope: disallow seller funds for down payment
cases.requiredGate: loan officer confirmation of funds-to-close structure
cases.riskIfWrong: The product could recommend an ineligible credit that fails underwriting.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC guidance does not allow interested-party contributions to satisfy reserve requirements.
cases.deal: Conventional purchase requiring reserves; seller offers credit to meet reserve condition.
expectedLeadScope: reserve funds cannot be replaced by seller IPC
cases.riskIfWrong: The output may misstate how reserves work and create a false path to approval.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC guidance treats financing concessions above borrower costs as sales concessions.
cases.deal: Conventional primary at 89 percent LTV; seller credit exceeds the final closing-cost worksheet.
cases.requiredGate: final fee worksheet and lender recalculation
cases.riskIfWrong: Loan terms may change late because the credit cannot simply remain unused.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC guidance treats non-realty giveaways differently from ordinary financing concessions.

inspection found working but old water heater
expectedExclusions: working but old water heater unless lender/appraiser flags condition

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC guidance identifies undisclosed interested-party contributions as loan-sale eligibility risk.

findings: repair credit not on settlement statement

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC guidance includes discount-point or rate-buydown costs funded by interested parties in concession math.

HVAC repair vs credit lender visibility

cases.requiredGate: loan officer fee worksheet after all credits

cases.deal: Conventional purchase of renovated property with prior garage fire.
findings: charred framing visible in attic over garage
cases.riskIfWrong: A credit for smoke odor can miss unrepaired structural collateral risk.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae property-condition guidance requires deficiencies affecting safety to be identified and potentially repaired.
cases.deal: Conventional purchase of older home with electrical system concerns.
expectedExclusions: vintage light switches if safe and operational
cases.requiredGate: licensed electrician report and lender acceptance
cases.riskIfWrong: The system may frame all old wiring as cosmetic or all vintage components as mandatory without evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae abnormal-settlement guidance can require a professional report or correction evidence.
cases.deal: Conventional primary in expansive-soil area.
findings: foundation piers visible at one corner
expectedExclusions: older roof gutters unless causing drainage/foundation issue
cases.riskIfWrong: A seller credit may not satisfy the lender if the appraisal references abnormal settlement.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae property-condition analysis can treat damaged pool barriers or structures as safety/marketability concerns.
cases.deal: Conventional primary with neglected pool.
findings: deep end covered by torn tarp
cases.riskIfWrong: The tool may only negotiate equipment value and leave a visible safety hazard unresolved.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae site-utility guidance requires durable access and maintenance rights for off-site private utility systems.
cases.deal: Conventional purchase with shared well and septic easements crossing a family parcel.
findings: septic force main crosses private land
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may draft condition repairs while title/utility access remains unsolved.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae C6/safety analysis can be triggered by missing finishes when they create unsafe or uninhabitable conditions, not mere decor issues.
cases.deal: Conventional primary; seller removed flooring after contract.
cases.riskIfWrong: The answer may either over-call decor items or under-call exposed subfloor safety issues.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae and government loan appraisal rules can override an as-is contract when lender-visible repairs affect collateral eligibility.
cases.persona: Buyer agent on as-is financed deal
cases.deal: Conventional as-is contract; buyer expects seller credit instead of repairs.
expectedExclusions: assuming as-is waives lender collateral conditions
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may believe negotiation rights are the only issue while financing cannot close without repair evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Industry repair-credit guidance and lender practice distinguish repair wording that reveals unresolved collateral defects from neutral closing-cost credits.
cases.persona: Buyer agent asking for credit language
cases.deal: Conventional buyer wants $8,000 because inspector found roof damage.
findings: draft says seller credit for roof replacement
lender has not reviewed repair issue
buyer asks to avoid lender questions
expectedExclusions: wording intended to hide known collateral defect
cases.requiredGate: loan officer and escrow wording approval
cases.riskIfWrong: The tool could encourage concealment or draft language that triggers underwriting conditions without repair plan.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae undisclosed IPC guidance and closing-disclosure rules make post-closing cash-back arrangements high risk.
cases.deal: Financed buyer; seller offers to Venmo repair money after closing.
cases.riskIfWrong: The output could facilitate mortgage fraud or an unsalable loan.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/Fannie Mae appraisal practice distinguishes repair escrow or completed repairs from simple credits when required repairs affect eligibility.
cases.deal: FHA buyer; seller wants to escrow funds for broken water heater after closing.
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may imply any credit works, although lender-required repairs usually need completion or approved escrow.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/HUD seller contribution guidance generally caps interested-party help and treats excess as an inducement or loan-amount issue.
cases.deal: FHA buyer already has 6 percent seller concessions and now asks for additional repair credit.
expectedLeadScope: price reduction or completed repair alternatives
expectedExclusions: assuming extra credit can stack above cap
cases.requiredGate: FHA lender concession and repair-condition review
cases.riskIfWrong: The amendment may exceed allowable credits and still fail to cure the lender-required repair.

cases.sourceBasis: VA concession guidance separates unlimited ordinary closing-cost credits from the 4 percent concession bucket for certain benefits.
cases.deal: VA buyer asks for closing costs, funding fee, and prepaid taxes in one sentence.
findings: buyer also asks for carpet allowance
expectedLeadScope: track funding fee/prepaids against 4 percent concession cap
expectedExclusions: treating every seller-paid dollar as the same category
cases.requiredGate: VA lender fee and concession worksheet
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may wrongly cap valid closing-cost help or approve excessive concessions.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac IPC and commission guidance requires separating customary buyer-agent compensation from true seller credits, especially with low investment-property caps.
cases.deal: Conventional investment property with seller-paid buyer-agent fee and 2 percent seller credit.
expectedLeadScope: no extra credit without lender math
expectedExclusions: assuming buyer-agent compensation always consumes IPC cap
assuming it never matters to lender
cases.riskIfWrong: The deal may either leave credit capacity unused or exceed a strict investment-property limit.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae IPC limits are based on lower-of value concepts and can interact with low appraisal and LTV recalculation.
cases.deal: Conventional primary; appraisal came in $20,000 low and seller proposes a credit instead of price reduction.
expectedLeadScope: seller credit cap after value change
expectedExclusions: minor GFCI issue unless appraisal/lender safety condition
cases.requiredGate: re-run underwriting with updated value and credits
cases.riskIfWrong: A mathematically attractive credit can be disallowed or reduce eligibility when value drops.

cases.sourceBasis: Lender-visible inspection defects can trigger appraisal or underwriting conditions when disclosed without a repair plan.
cases.persona: Buyer agent deciding what to send lender
cases.deal: FHA buyer; full inspection report includes major safety defects and cosmetic notes.
cases.requiredGate: loan officer guidance on disclosure and repair conditions
cases.riskIfWrong: The output may advise broad report sharing or hiding without managing lender-required repair consequences.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA/VA appraisal processes often require reinspection when utilities were unavailable or required repairs are completed after initial visit.
cases.deal: VA buyer; appraisal occurred with water off and seller says it can be turned on next week.
findings: buyer closing date in six days
expectedExclusions: assuming appraisal is final despite unobserved systems
cases.riskIfWrong: The product may miss a timeline-critical second visit and misadvise on closing readiness.

cases.sourceBasis: FHA, VA, and conventional appraisal-condition workflows require completion evidence for required repairs rather than unsupported seller promises.
cases.deal: FHA buyer; seller signs amendment promising repairs before closing.
findings: missing handrail to be installed by seller
peeling exterior paint to be corrected
seller provides no receipts or photos yet
expectedLeadScope: appraiser final inspection or lender signoff
cases.riskIfWrong: The buyer may reach closing without evidence needed to clear lender-required repair conditions.
